I2408.bp: parish of St Jean de Sanac diocese

ev.p: parish of St Jean de Sanac diocese

notes: Birth date: the headstone record gives 19 Jan 1846, which fits his age of 52 at death on 4 Dec 1898. Family trees give 18 Jan or 18 Nov 1847. The headstone date is shown.

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• No record naming his parents was reachable. Ancestry (genealogy/records pages), Find a Grave, FamilySearch records, NYS Historic Newspapers and fultonhistory.com all refused automated access, and web search returned nothing for his Toledo obituary, marriage or census households. Not opened: https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/william-a-french-24-2p0f5tp (lists 1870 and 1880 census and 'NY Extracted Death Index' matches - viewing those by hand is the fastest next step).
• Birth-date conflict not settled by any new record. The only internal check: the existing bio gives age 52 at death on 4 Dec 1898, which fits the headstone date 19 Jan 1846 (52 yrs 10 mos) and not 18 Nov 1847 (51) or 18 Jan 1847 (51). Note the tree's own field says 18 JAN 1847 while the Ancestry page says 11/18/1847 - one of those is a transposition.
• Order/look up: (1) Lucas County Probate Court death register, Dec 1898 (pre-1908 Ohio deaths were recorded by the county; FamilySearch 'Ohio, County Death Records, 1840-2001') - gives age, birthplace, occupation and sometimes parents; (2) Toledo Blade and Toledo Bee, 5-6 Dec 1898, via Toledo Lucas County Public Library obituary index (the same library supplied the 1899 McKenna clipping); (3) Forest Cemetery lot card for Section R lot 86 (lot owner and all burials); (4) 1870 census Syracuse and 1875 NY state census Onondaga County (the 1875 state census gives county of birth); (5) Boyd's Syracuse directories 1868-1882 (FamilySearch catalog 2494645) for his occupation and address, then anyone named French at the same address.
• Candidate French households in Onondaga County, unproven: Child's Gazetteer and Business Directory of Onondaga County 1868-9 lists 'French, Edward, (Kirkville,) lots 48 and 57, farmer 157' in the town of Manlius - the same town where the McKennas were living in 1850 - plus 'French David, patent sidewalk manufacturer, 380 E. Genesee' in Syracuse, 'French, William, (Cardiff,) lot 72, farmer' in Lafayette, Hazen M., Russel C. and Stephen French at Summit Station, and Asbel, Asbel Jr. and Gilbert R. French in Otisco. Nothing ties William A. to any of them yet; check Edward French of Kirkville's 1850/1855/1860 households for a son William aged about 4, 9 and 14. Source: https://archive.org/stream/gazetteerbusinesocny00chil/gazetteerbusinesocny00chil_djvu.txt
• The USGenWeb 1850 Onondaga County census transcription (us-census.org) is only partial (about 8 page-files). Its only French household is Joseph 24, Julia 21, Mahitable 3, Charles H. 4/12, with Ashvill French 19 nearby (pages 310b-311b, file pg0306b.txt), all born New York; no William, and no Felix McKenna in the transcribed pages. https://www.us-census.org/pub/usgenweb/census/ny/onondaga/1850/indx-f-j.txt

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• Not researched beyond one web search (no result). 1880 Putnam County history says Mary Kathrina Beckmann was born in Prussia 26 May 1851 (tree has 28 Mar 1851). Her 8 Jun 1936 Ohio death certificate (Lucas Co.) should name parents.

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• Parents not found. Next: (1) his Civil War pension file (Co. F, 100th Ohio Inf.; widow predeceased, so an invalid pension) at NARA, which normally states birthplace and often family; (2) Lucas County marriage record c.1857-58 (FamilySearch catalog https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog/312294, Lucas County marriages 1835-1985); (3) Lucas County death record/Toledo Blade obituary for 25 Sep 1904; (4) 1900 census Toledo/Maumee for year of immigration; (5) page image of the Ohio Roster vol. 7 (https://archive.org/details/officialrosterof07ohio) for his age at enlistment and discharge remarks. 'Born Montreal' probably means the Montréal district; with no parents' names a Drouin baptism cannot be picked from the many Joseph (Audet dit) Lapointe born 1835-36.
• Unrelated same-name people checked and rejected: John Bt. LaPoint of Erie, Monroe Co., MI (WikiTree La_Pointe-38, bapt. 1776); Joseph LaPoint Jr. of Bayfield, WI; Joseph Lapointe of Leeds-Grenville, Ontario. The earlier bio's Niagara County/Syracuse association appears to be wrong for this man.

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• Resolve Harris vs Sterling: the Wiltsee memoir (1908) says Jacob's wife was a Sterling of Spencertown, Columbia County, NY, b. 1 Feb 1750, d. 19 Feb 1830; the local historical society says 'Esther Harris (or Sterling)'. Read the shared Wiltse gravestone in Springfield Township Cemetery (Holland, Ohio) for her death date and age, and check Spencertown/Claverack Dutch Reformed and Hillsdale records for a Sterling or Harris marriage to Jacob Wiltse about 1778-1780. Her husband Jacob Wiltse (I2516) has documented parents if not already in the tree: Cornelius Wiltse Jr. and Elizabeth Cornell (both sources).
Was a patriot of the American Revolution.

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• Caution: Cornell Genealogy p.163-164 is unsure whether the Elizabeth Cornell who married Cornelius Wiltse on 5 Jan 1748/9 was the daughter of William and Charity Doughty (bap. 30 Jul 1732) or of William's brother Thomas and Mary Kissam (bap. 6 Oct 1734). The SAR application in the tree uses 30 Jul 1732, i.e. William's daughter. Either way the line runs through William (1668-1743) and Richard of Rockaway. Father's will (dated 1756, proved 1781) mentions daughter Elizabeth - the full will (NY wills liber 34) may give her married name and settle it.

Next steps (research pass, Nov 2026):
• Parents still unknown. Best lead: the Barnes family that migrated with the Wiltses from Sterling, Cayuga County - Josiah or Joshua Barnes (died before 1823) married Ann Wiltse, John Wiltse's sister, so Joannah (b. 1792) was not his daughter but may be his sister or cousin; a Jacob Barnes was selling land in Springfield Township in 1831. Look for Barnes households in Cato/Sterling/Hannibal in the 1800 and 1810 censuses, Storke's History of Cayuga County (1879) Sterling chapter, and Hallie DeMass Sweeting's 'Pioneers of Sterling, NY'. The tree's 'Rochester or Oswego' birthplace is not supported by anything found (Rochester did not exist in 1792).
